sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 2024. Engan fringe languages (North and South). Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 42: 94-110.
sources.note: Nothing. Fn.5 p.95: 'On some SIL wordlists Nete is also called Pikaru or Bikaru. Bisorio is sometimes also listed as Iniai.' Lexical comparison of Bisorio/Iniai, Pikaru and Sau; cites unpublished SIL wordlists (Dye 1967 Bisorio, Iniai; Pikaru #1/#2 1983; Edmiston 1986).

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. Newguineaworld: Bisorio (Nete-Bisorio, Trans-Enga). Last modified 2024-06-25.
sources.note: 'There is no published phonology of Bisorio.' Sources named: Davies & Comrie 1985 (66 terms after Wayne Dye) and Conrad & Lewis 1988 (106 terms for Pikaru of Piame village and Bisorio after Bob Kennell, New Tribes Mission).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (submitted by Devin O'Bannon, SIL-PNG, with Robert Conrad). 2020. Change Request 2020-026: merge [bic] Bikaru into [bir] Bisorio (adopted 2021-01-15).
sources.note: Nothing. States that Bragge's wordlist 'was a poor elicitation' (22% cognate with Pikaru 1) and that Pikaru is 'possibly above 90% cognate with Bisorio'; the only published source cited is Conrad & Lewis 1988.

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & Ron Lewis. 1988. Some language and sociolinguistic relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26, 243-273. Pacific Linguistics A-76.
sources.note: Nothing. pp.249-250: Pikaru (Bikaru, Bigalu) is 'the least-known language of the entire survey'; Bragge's Bikaru list (Ambunti patrol report 4/70-71) is only 22% cognate with their Pikaru 1 list; Pikaru is a dialect of Bisorio (Enga sub-family). Fig. 8 (App. 9.2) reprints the 'Bikaru (Bragge)' wordlist with no stress marking; transcriptions assumed 'approximately phonemic' (p.245).

sources.citation: Davies, John & Bernard Comrie. 1985. A linguistic survey of the Upper Yuat. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 22, 275-312. Pacific Linguistics A-63.
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical survey; Bisorio and Iniai wordlists by Wayne Dye (SIL) reproduced 'in their original form' in the Appendix (pp.283ff); the Iniai list carries apostrophes (apparently SIL stress marks) but no statement about stress anywhere; Bikaru not mentioned.

sources.citation: New Tribes Mission. 1982. Bisorio Genesis translation (Senesise). Rosetta Project archive.org item rosettaproject_bir_gen-1.
sources.note: Nothing; scripture text in practical orthography (Bisorio, not Bikaru).

sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. 1975. Comments on Proto-Engan. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 263-276. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Nothing on Bikaru/Bisorio (neither name occurs). Only a general remark (p.270) that phonemic tone and vowel length in Engan languages were not discussed and that tone 'often disambiguates present day minimal pairs'.

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25.
sources.note: Nothing. Entry 110 BIKARU (Bigalu), p.32: villages uncensused; based only on a wordlist in Bragge's patrol report 4/70-71 of Ambunti; tentatively classified with Sepik Hill languages 'pending further data'. No phonological remarks.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1/5.3 reference list for Bisorio (biso1243) and Ethnologue/Wikipedia Bisorio pages.
sources.note: Bisorio has no grammar, sketch or phonology doctype in Glottolog (refs: Davies & Comrie 1985, Franklin 1975, Conrad & Lewis 1988, Laycock 1973, ISO CR 2020-026, Franklin 2024, Ethnologue 18, Haberland 1963 wordlist ms.). Wikipedia (Ethnologue-derived): 'Bikaru... is a dialect of Bisorio fully mutually intelligible with the rest of the language'; no phonology.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3. Bookkeeping: Bikaru-Bragge (bika1251).
sources.note: Nothing. 'This entry has been retired and is featured here only for bookkeeping purposes'; retired in ISO 639-3, merged into [bir] Bisorio, CR 2020-026. No descriptive references.

sources.citation: Rosetta Project. n.d. Bikaru Swadesh List [bic]. archive.org item rosettaproject_bic_swadesh-1.
sources.note: Nothing. Forms (arrow bawi, ashes heme, back makia, bad ali, belly wafei, bird bamuwi, day lowu, child nauwa) are the 'Bikaru (Bragge)' column of Conrad & Lewis 1988 Fig. 8; no stress marks, no source note.
